Thanks Soojin — quick read of the SPSA and summary. Initial legal guidance below. I attached a single-file markup of the standard MSA flow-down clause with inline comments; these are my asks to cover both the Order Form and DPA annex.

High-level legal asks (must-haves):
1) Audit / access: add explicit audit rights for Redwood and its auditors to review EdgeOps' controls; require 30 days' notice for on-site audits and reasonable cooperation.
2) Data residency: ensure Order Form includes a binding EEA-only processing restriction for any EU-sourced customer data (EdgeOps to keep within EU AZs for that customer's data).
3) Sub-subprocessing: require pre-notification + right to object for any further subcontracting (i.e., EdgeOps must list sub-subprocessors and obtain our consent for any that process EEA data).
4) Security evidence: request SOC 2 Type II (last 12 months), encryption key management description (who manages KMS/HSM), and a recent pen-test summary. Redact full reports if necessary; we accept a redacted SOC with auditor signature.
5) Indemnity & limitation: preserve MSA indemnity for data breach caused by subprocessor; reject attempts to eliminate that carveout.

Negotiable items (procurement to weigh):
- Price delta for managed service: acceptable to procurement if vendor tiering is Tier 2 and there's a fixed 90-day pilot credit.
- PO amendment mechanics: procurement can authorize a PO change once legal confirms SOW/orderform language.

If the vendor can provide the SOC and key management doc within 5 business days we can do a limited scoped approval for pilot (documented and time-boxed to 90 days). If not, we trigger formal redline and add to escalation.
